chapter: Dreamland and the Tuxedo dance hall
title: Bringing Oscar Silvestre into the Tuxedo band
summary: He tells how a trumpet player quit and he persuaded George Filhe and the boss to hire Silvestre, a railroad worker and Jack Carey man, and how the first night went.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, we had a fellow in the band. I know him with Foyer. He was a very fine trumpet player. First triple-tone solo. And he was a fellow. He was out and down. He loved to play Koch. He loved it Koch. Well, he had him on the job. He was on the job about two months, something like that. Got his pocket filled full of money. We played there. Time would knock off, seven, eight o'clock in the morning. Some champagne drinkers come, time, knock off, there they come in while we stay. and we would all go home. He would go to twenty-fives. He would go there and sit down twenty-five until two or three o'clock that evening playing Koch. Now he would go home, he had very little sleep. He followed that pace until he couldn't hold up no more. Then he laid off. He was allowed a trumpet player for three weeks. And like all the big New York people used to come to hear that band, he always says, well, where's the trumpet player? All right. Harry always tried to say, Harry, what's that trumpet player?
